subject: Payment hold — conflicting request_id counts on June billing window
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CacheFleet payment hold — conflicting request_id counts

Hi Maya / Kim —

Collections put CacheFleet's June invoice on hold this morning. They flagged a mismatch between our token export and the request_id stream they provided: their side shows ~18.6M unique request_ids in the billing window while our exported token attribution shows ~19.9M attributed tokens (same window). CacheFleet's billing team is refusing to release payment until we provide an explanation and a reconciled sample.

They specifically called out a set of duplicate request_ids (same id appearing 2+ times in our export) which they say should have been deduplicated. Collections asked for: 
- a short (<=1000-row) sample of raw request_id -> token attribution logs for the window;
- a short writeup explaining how deduplication / replay handling was applied in our pipeline for the 2028-06 billing window;
- a suggested credit or corrected invoice if we confirm over-attribution.

I attached the slice they sent us (they redacted most rows), and Collections wants us to respond within 24 hours to avoid escalation to legal.

Can you confirm whether anything changed in the attribution pipeline around 2028-06-01? Markus, any known rekeying / prefix-hash change in the ingest path recently?

Thanks —
Ben
Collections | Redwood Inference
[attachment: cachefleet_requestid_dump_20280613.csv (CSV, 34KB)]

From: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CacheFleet payment hold — conflicting request_id counts

Thanks for the heads up, Ben.

Quick summary from my side after a first-pass look: we rolled a change into the ingest prefix hashing on 2028-06-01 that changes how duplicate request_ids are normalized when requests arrive from different edge POPs. The change was intended to reduce false de-duplication for long-lived streaming sessions, but it also altered the dedupe key composition for a narrow set of customers that send request_ids without stable host prefixes.

I am attaching a 500-row sample pulled from our token attribution export (redwood_token_export_sample_20280613.json) that includes: request_id, arrival_ts, edge_pop, dedupe_key, and token_count. In that sample you can see a handful of request_ids that appear twice with different dedupe_key values (different edge_pop -> different hash), which explains why our exported attribution shows higher unique hits than CacheFleet's internal dump (they dedupe by request_id only).

Hypothesis: CacheFleet's client SDK sets request_id per-log-entry (same id) but sometimes proxies through different POPs; our new hashing unintentionally made the requests look distinct.

Action plan proposals (pick one):
1) Quick credit: retroactively dedupe by request_id for their June billing window and issue a one-time credit (estimated token reduction: ~7.8%). I can run the exact tally and provide a proposed credit amount within 3 hours.
2) Short-term correction: recalculate their June invoice with request_id-only deduplication and issue an adjusted invoice + DocuSign credit form.
3) Stick with current attribution, explain the change, ask CacheFleet to update SDK/proxies to preserve host prefix (longer-term).

I recommend option 2 to unblock payment and keep the customer relationship smooth. If Collections prefers option 1 for speed, we can do that, but we'll need engineering to run the dedupe job and provide token count delta.

Markus — can you confirm how fast we can produce a deterministic re-count for the month if we run request_id-only dedupe? Also any downstream accounting implications (ledger rekeying)?

— Maya
Product Sales Ops | Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood_token_export_sample_20280613.json (JSON, 120KB)]

From: Asha Patel <asha@cachefleet.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>
Cc: CacheFleet Billing <billing@cachefleet.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CacheFleet payment hold — conflicting request_id counts

Maya / Ben —

Thanks for the quick investigation. We've attached the small request_id dump that Collections referenced (same file Ben attached) and a slightly larger extract from our side (cachefleet_requestid_dump_20280613.csv) that shows the duplicate ids in our logs — you can filter on column "request_id" to see unique counts.

CacheFleet will not release the outstanding $128,340 invoice until we receive either: 
- an adjusted invoice showing the corrected token total and VAT treatment, plus a signed credit memorandum (DocuSign link OK); or
- a written explanation that shows there is no overcharge and why (we will escalate internally if we still see a discrepancy).

We're open to the request_id-only dedupe approach as a pragmatic fix, but two asks: 
1) Please confirm whether the correction will affect VAT accounting (we need to know if the credit will be gross vs net for our EU entity).
2) Provide a timeline for when we can expect a corrected invoice and a DocuSign-ready credit form — our payable team has a cutoff on Friday EOD (2028-06-16) to clear anything in this cycle.

Please include the exact token delta and the adjusted USD value in your reply.

Regards,
Asha Patel
Head of Platform | CacheFleet Inc.
[attachment: cachefleet_requestid_dump_20280613.csv (CSV, 147KB)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha@cachefleet.com>, CacheFleet Billing <billing@cachefleet.com>
Cc: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CacheFleet payment hold — conflicting request_id counts

Hi Asha —

Thanks for sending the dump and for the patience. We validated Maya's hypothesis and ran a request_id-only re-aggregation for CacheFleet's June billing window. Findings: 
- Original invoice token total: 19,892,411 tokens
- Request_id-only deduped token total: 18,354,984 tokens
- Token delta: 1,537,427 tokens (~7.73% reduction)
- USD impact (using your contracted rate): $9,460.88 credit (gross).

VAT treatment: the credit will be issued gross and follow the same VAT treatment as the original invoice for your EU entity. Our finance team will include a VAT/credit memorandum that you can attach to your books.

Next steps we propose: 
1) We will issue an adjusted invoice reflecting the corrected token total and a credit memo. Link to the provisional invoice/credit: https://app.redwood.com/invoices/DF-3742/adjusted
2) Attached is the adjusted invoice PDF and a DocuSign link to sign the credit memorandum: https://na1.docusign.net/DocuSign/transaction/ABC12345
3) Once signed, Collections will lift the hold and your payable team can process the outstanding balance.

If that works, we can get the DocuSign executed and have Collections confirm release to your payable team today so you can hit your Friday cutoff.

Apologies for the disruption — we're also flagging this with Engineering to avoid similar rekeying side-effects in future releases.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
